name: BNZ
h1: When software ages faster, build tools that change faster
lede: BNZ has said AI is making its own software obsolete sooner. Airtable gives engineering, cyber and program teams configurable workflows beside the core platforms, without another large build.
why_h2: Faster change, tighter capital, more programs in flight
why_p: A software capitalisation reset, a one-off charge and new sustainability models all point to doing more with configurable, fast-to-change tooling.

signals.title: Software capitalisation policy reset
signals.body: BNZ shortened the useful life of capitalised software and raised the capitalisation threshold from $5M to $20M, reducing the balance by NZ$352M. It cited more frequent enhancements and faster obsolescence, including from increased AI adoption.
signals.angle: Configurable workflows around the core change as fast as the business does, without adding to the capitalised build list.

signals.title: Half-year statutory profit down 37.9%
signals.body: Statutory net profit for the half to 31 March 2026 was $494M, down 37.9%, driven by the one-off software adjustment. Excluding it, profit was $747M.
signals.angle: Cost discipline favours tools teams can configure themselves over new custom builds.

signals.title: Native forest carbon removal model with Pamu
signals.body: BNZ became first leaseholder on a 600 ha northern Hawke's Bay property under a native forest carbon removal model with Pamu, about 1,100 tCO2e a year.
signals.angle: New sustainability programs need a clear record of sites, partners and outcomes from day one.
